summary.whatHappened: From 2026-08-19T17:49:10Z to 18:01:05Z, mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com (caller IP 198.51.100.42) modified GCP project pocaas-prod-01. Actions included creating backdoor-svc-gcp@pocaas-prod-01.iam.gserviceaccount.com, creating a key for it, granting it roles/owner, opening an allow-all firewall, creating crypto-miner-01/02/03, reading confidential bucket objects financial-report-2026.xlsx, employee-pii-export.csv, and api-keys-production.json, deleting export-all-logs, disabling the _Default log sink, and granting itself roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on deploy-pipeline@pocaas-prod-01.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
keyEvidence: Audit log sequence ties mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com from 198.51.100.42 to service account creation, key creation, owner grant, and token-creator grant in pocaas-prod-01.
The new account name backdoor-svc-gcp and the created RSA key are persistent credential material.
Confidential objects were read from pocaas-confidential-data, showing real project access beyond setup.
Logging was tampered with by deleting export-all-logs and disabling _Default.
Web sources note GCP service account keys are persistent credentials and IAM policy/impersonation grants are used for cloud persistence (Google Cloud docs; Datadog Security Labs).
